content: Carrier oil, also referred to as base oil or vegetable oil, is specifically utilized to dilute essential oils and absolutes prior to their application on the skin. The term carrier is derived from their function of carrying essential oils onto the skin. Unlike essential oils, carrier oils do not possess a concentrated aroma and do not evaporate in the same manner. There is a wide variety of carrier oils available, each with unique properties that make them suitable for different therapeutic applications in aromatherapy. Infused oils are a blend of a carrier oil and various herbs. True carrier oils are typically cold-pressed vegetable oils derived from sources such as sweet almond, grapeseed, avocado, olive, sesame, evening primrose, sunflower, jojoba, and emu oil. Additionally, carrier oils can be extracted from nuts, including walnut, peanut, pecan, and macadamia nut, as well as fractionated coconut oil. Among these, sweet almond oil and grapeseed oil are the most commonly used carrier oils.
